mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts contraction (HOUST < previous 6-month average) signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST < 6M moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE > 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO < previous 12-month average for four consecutive months) signals supply-side weakness, which compresses profit margins and drags on equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of INDPRO contraction relative to the prior 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS drops by > 1 percentage point in one month) signals an emergency monetary easing in response to financial stress, which boosts risk appetite and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during episodes of FEDFUNDS dropping > 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month signals accelerating labor market deterioration, which reduces earnings and consumer demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases AND PAYEMS decreases > -0.5% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during episodes of simultaneous UNRATE rise and PAYEMS drop > -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1 > 4% YoY growth) alongside rising housing starts (HOUST > previous 12-month average) signals robust aggregate demand expansion, which supports earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 4% AND HOUST > 12M moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of GDPC1 > 4% YoY growth and elevated HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent inflation surge (CPIAUCSL > 6% for four consecutive months) in the absence of a corresponding rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 3% for the same period) signals monetary policy lag, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 6% for four consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS < 3% for the same period
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during four consecutive months of CPIAUCSL > 6% with FEDFUNDS < 3%.
